en: 3 Extinction
zh: 3　灭绝

en: Extinction constitutes our second analytical entry point into plantation lifeworlds and afterlives. While intrinsically connected to extraction in terms of its dynamics and effects, extinction draws attention to the forms of

that have historically accompanied monocrop proliferation and whose legacies remain embedded in the landscapes of the present – even where these landscapes may no longer be classified or exploited as agro-industrial zones. In this section, I examine how plantation-driven species and ecosystemic extinctions sit within, and further, a broader process of ecological decline and climate crisis, wherein industrial and human activities are undermining conditions of life at a planetary scale (Chao & Kirksey 2022). I consider how environmental destruction erodes the intimate and ancestral biocultural relations and multispecies histories binding peoples, plants, and places. In doing so, I follow the lead of environmental humanities scholars in approaching extinction not as a one-off ‘event’, marked by the passing of the last individual of a species, but rather as a loss that sits within broader patterns of unravelling and that entails the erasure of ways of life shared across species lines – including with humans (van Dooren 2014; Rose & van Dooren 2017). In closing, I consider the promise and perils of corporate sustainability and conservation initiatives that seek to greenify the plantation sector but run counter to the ways of knowing, being, and relating that communities entertain with non-human lifeforms and landscapes, thus perpetuating, in a different guise, the colonial logic of the plantation itself.
zh: 灭绝构成我们理解种植园生活世界及其后续存续的第二个分析入口。虽然它在动态过程和影响方面与攫取有着内在联系，灭绝更把注意力引向种种破坏、灭除、丧失与毁败：它们在历史上伴随着单一种植的扩散，其遗产至今仍嵌入当下的景观之中——即使这些景观可能已不再被归类为或用作农工业地带。在本部分，我考察种植园驱动的物种灭绝与生态系统消亡，如何置身于并加剧更广泛的生态衰败与气候危机；在这一过程中，工业和人类活动正在行星尺度上削弱生命得以存续的条件（Chao & Kirksey 2022）。我将思考，环境破坏如何侵蚀联结人群、植物与地方的亲密且世代相传的生物—文化关系和多物种历史。为此，我沿着环境人文学者的思路，将灭绝理解为更广泛的瓦解模式之中的一种丧失，而非以某个物种最后一个个体的死亡为标志、一次性发生的“事件”。这种丧失，意味着跨越物种界线——也包括人类——共同分享的生活方式被抹除（van Dooren 2014；Rose & van Dooren 2017）。最后，我将考察企业可持续性倡议与自然保护倡议的希望及危险。这些倡议试图使种植园产业绿色化，却与社群同非人生命形式和景观之间的认识方式、存在方式及关系方式相冲突，从而换一种面貌，延续种植园自身的殖民逻辑。

en: 3.1 Biodiversity Loss and the Climate Crisis
zh: 3.1　生物多样性丧失与气候危机

en: As production systems that often entail major land-use changes, industrial plantations constitute primary drivers of deforestation, biodiversity loss, and the erosion of vital ecosystem functions including carbon storage, soil regeneration, and air and water quality. Their proliferation drives almost 50 per cent of global forest loss, with carbon released into the atmosphere from plantation-driven deforestation accounting for around 10 per cent of global warming emissions. These impacts are symptomatic of, and directly contribute to, the broader phenomenon of climate change, which is reconfiguring the terrains and topographies of multispecies existence across an increasingly vulnerable and volatile planet.
zh: 工业化种植园作为常常涉及重大土地利用变化的生产体系，是毁林、生物多样性丧失，以及碳储存、土壤再生、空气与水质等关键生态系统功能遭侵蚀的主要驱动因素。种植园扩张推动了全球近50%的森林丧失；种植园驱动的毁林所释放到大气中的碳，约占导致全球变暖的排放总量的10%。这些影响体现了更广泛的气候变化现象，也直接促成了气候变化。在一个日益脆弱、动荡的星球上，气候变化正重塑多物种存在的地域与地形。
body.review: 本段50%与10%的归因范围依底本保留。后文所引忧思科学家联盟2016年资料，把超过一半的热带毁林归于牛肉、大豆、棕榈油和木制品四类商品，把约10%的温室气体排放归于毁林总体；两者均不直接等于单独由种植园造成的全球比例。

en: The oil palm industry is a case in point. Oil palm, or

Jacquin in Linnean taxonomy, thrives best in humid lowland environments, and particularly in riverine forests and freshwater swamps. Shade-intolerant and hydrophilic, the plant requires high levels of soil moisture, temperatures ranging from 24 to 32 degrees Celsius, and at least 1,780 to 2,280 millimetres of rain per year. These factors combined make the planet’s tropical belt the ideal environment for oil palm cultivation. However, it is also in these same tropical zones that the highest levels of biodiversity today are to be found, and where the most rapid rates of species extinction are underway (Qaim et al. 2020; Chao 2022d). Today, palm oil is one of just four commodities driving the majority of tropical deforestation (up to half, according to some reports) and oil palm plantations represent the second largest driver of global warming after beef production (Union of Concerned Scientists 2016). Between 2000 and 2010 alone, oil palm monocrops were responsible for 2–9 per cent of worldwide emissions from tropical land use (Carlson & Curran 2013). Most of these emission stem from Indonesia and Malaysia, who together produce over 80 per cent of the world’s palm oil supplies.
zh: 油棕产业就是一例。油棕，在林奈分类体系中名为Elaeis guineensis Jacquin，最适宜生长在潮湿的低地环境，尤其是河岸森林与淡水沼泽。它不耐阴且喜水，需要较高的土壤湿度、24至32摄氏度的温度，以及每年至少1,780至2,280毫米的降雨。这些因素结合起来，使地球的热带带区成为栽培油棕的理想环境。然而，也恰恰是在这些热带地区，今天的生物多样性最为丰富，物种灭绝的速度也最快（Qaim et al. 2020；Chao 2022d）。如今，大部分热带毁林仅由四类商品推动，棕榈油就是其中之一（据一些报告，比例高达一半）；而油棕种植园，是仅次于牛肉生产的全球变暖第二大驱动因素（Union of Concerned Scientists 2016）。仅在2000年至2010年间，油棕单一种植就造成了全球热带土地利用排放的2%—9%（Carlson & Curran 2013）。这些排放大多来自印度尼西亚和马来西亚；两国合计供应全球80%以上的棕榈油。
body.review: “全球变暖第二大驱动因素”为底本原句。所引忧思科学家联盟2016年网页的语境，是比较导致热带毁林的主要商品及其排放，并非把棕榈油排在所有全球变暖来源的第二位；不应据此排除化石燃料等其他来源。底本“Most of these emission”的单复数问题保留于英文。

en: The establishment of plantations on carbon-rich peatlands in Southeast Asia plays a major role in the story of oil palm-driven multispecies extinctions and ecosystemic destruction. Peatlands may release up to twenty-eight times as much carbon as the forests above them when drained for agricultural purposes, requiring more than 600 years for the carbon balance to be re-established (Danielsen et al. 2009). Easily ignited following drainage and difficult to extinguish, predict, and control, peat fires can last for weeks or even months, smouldering subterraneously over vast areas and sometimes re-emerging miles away from their initial source (Page & Hooijer 2016). The flammability of peatlands is exacerbated by concentrated cash crop planting, which over time reduces freshwater and soil quality, undermines critical ecosystem services once sustained by forests such as regulation of the hydrological cycle and soil protection, and overall enhances the risk of abiotic effects, including intensified wind, desiccation, and fire risk. Gradually, soil erosion and nutrient and mineral depletion undermine the very grounds of the plantation, together with the other-than-human communities of life that inhabit and depend upon them.
zh: 在东南亚富含碳的泥炭地上建立种植园，在油棕驱动的多物种灭绝与生态系统破坏过程中，占据重要位置。泥炭地为农业用途而排水后，释放的碳量可能高达其上方森林的二十八倍，碳平衡则需要六百多年才能重新建立（Danielsen et al. 2009）。排水后的泥炭地容易被点燃，火势又难以扑灭、预测和控制；泥炭火灾可持续数周甚至数月，在广大地区的地下阴燃，有时会在距离最初火源数英里外重新冒出地面（Page & Hooijer 2016）。经济作物的密集种植，使泥炭地更易燃烧。随着时间推移，密集种植会降低淡水与土壤质量，削弱森林原本维持的关键生态系统服务，如水循环调节与土壤保护，并在总体上增加非生物因素带来的风险，包括风力增强、干燥和火灾危险。逐渐地，土壤侵蚀以及养分、矿物的耗竭，侵蚀了种植园自身赖以存在的基础，也损害了栖居其间并依赖这些基础的非人生命共同体。

en: The simplified ecology of monocrop oil palm plantations proves a largely inhospitable environment for those organisms who manage to survive the felling and flames. This ecology is characterized by uniform tree species and tree age structure, low canopies, sparse understory vegetation, low-stability microclimates, the almost-complete absence of leaf litter, a twenty-five to thirty-year clearing cycle, and run-off from chemical fertilizers and pesticides (Obidzinski et al. 2012; Petrenko et al. 2016). Habitat fragmentation, the shift to simpler community compositions, the absence of ecological corridors, and the impervious barriers posed by plantations to animal migration undermine both species richness and abundance, allowing only about 15 per cent of native vertebrate animal species to survive the transition from primary forest to plantation, and fewer than half of vertebrate communities (Fitzherbert et al. 2008; Savilaakso et al. 2014). As a result, palm oil production is adversely affecting at least 193 threatened species globally, according to the International Union for the Conservation of Nature Red List of Threatened Species. These species encompass 54 per cent of all threatened mammals and 64 per cent of all threatened birds globally (Meijaard et al. 2018). Among the most vulnerable to forest-monocrop landscape transitions and associated heightened poaching activities and human-wildlife conflicts are the critically endangered Bornean and Sumatran orangutans, the Sumatran tiger, the Sumatran rhinoceros, and the Sumatran and Bornean pygmy elephants, alongside forest specialist species such as the muscicapine flycatcher, the arboreal fruit-eating gibbon, and the peat swamp frog.
zh: 对于那些在砍伐与烈焰中幸存下来的生物而言，单一油棕种植园经过简化的生态，仍是一个大体上难以栖居的环境。这种生态的特征包括：树种与树龄结构单一、树冠低矮、林下植被稀疏、小气候稳定性较低、几乎没有凋落叶层、二十五至三十年一次的清除周期，以及化肥和农药随径流流失（Obidzinski et al. 2012；Petrenko et al. 2016）。栖息地破碎化、群落组成趋于简单、生态廊道缺失，以及种植园为动物迁徙设下的难以穿透的障碍，削弱了物种丰富度与丰度。在从原生林向种植园转变的过程中，仅约15%的本土脊椎动物物种得以存续，脊椎动物群落则不到一半（Fitzherbert et al. 2008；Savilaakso et al. 2014）。因此，根据国际自然保护联盟《濒危物种红色名录》，棕榈油生产正对全球至少193种受威胁物种产生不利影响。这些物种涵盖了全球所有受威胁哺乳动物的54%，以及所有受威胁鸟类的64%（Meijaard et al. 2018）。在森林转变为单一种植景观，并伴随着偷猎活动加剧和人兽冲突增多的过程中，最脆弱的物种包括极危的婆罗洲猩猩与苏门答腊猩猩、苏门答腊虎、苏门答腊犀，以及苏门答腊象和婆罗洲侏儒象；还包括鹟类、树栖食果的长臂猿和泥炭沼泽蛙等依赖特定森林生境的物种。
body.review: 193种与54%／64%不是同一统计口径。IUCN2018年说明将193种列为已受棕榈油生产影响的受威胁物种，而54%／64%指适宜未来油棕扩张地区中、可能受到影响的受威胁哺乳动物与鸟类比例。本书将其写成同一组物种的现有涵盖比例，译文保留并指出差异。前句两项脊椎动物比例及各物种等级，仍需对照所引原研究的样本与年份。

en: The soy industry is another key driver of biodiversity loss, its expansion contributing to 8.2 million hectares of forest replacement between 2001 and 2015 and representing over 10 per cent of tropical deforestation tied to agricultural commodities during that period (World Resources Institute 2024). The proliferation of this crop is particularly marked in Latin America, notably in Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay, Bolivia, and Uruguay, where over half of the world’s soybean production takes place, and where the perceived availability of cheaper tropical lands is legitimating the expansion of soy as a source of beans, oil, and meal for human and livestock consumption, and as a source of renewable energy (Song et al. 2021).
zh: 大豆产业是生物多样性丧失的另一个重要驱动力。2001年至2015年间，其扩张促成了八百二十万公顷森林被替代，占同期与农业商品相关的热带毁林的10%以上（World Resources Institute 2024）。这种作物的扩散，在拉丁美洲尤其显著，特别是巴西、阿根廷、巴拉圭、玻利维亚和乌拉圭。全球一半以上的大豆产自这里；人们认为这里存在价格更低、可供利用的热带土地，于是为大豆扩张赋予正当性，把它作为供人类与牲畜消费的豆粒、豆油和豆粕的来源，也作为可再生能源的来源（Song et al. 2021）。

en: In Brazil, soy plantations are concentrated in ecologically sensitive regions such as the Amazon, where mass-cultivated areas increased fourfold from 1.14 million hectares in 2006 to 4.48 million hectares in 2016, and the Cerrado, which is home to some of the most biodiverse savanna landscapes in the world (Sauer 2018; Schneider et al. 2021). Unlike the Amazon, the Cerrado lies outside the zones protected by the 2006 Soy Moratorium, a voluntary pact intended to reduce deforestation caused directly by soy (Brandão, Cardoso & Garrett 2025). The region has suffered a 50 per cent loss in native vegetation due to monocrop developments in the last two decades, leading to the critical endangerment of thousands of endemic plants and animals, including the maned wolf, giant anteater, blue-eyed ground dove, and white-nosed saki. In tandem, slash-and-burn methods used to clear land for soy contribute to degraded air quality and greenhouse gas emissions, at the same time as they render fragmented forests increasingly vulnerable to fire. The leaching of agrochemicals into rivers, waterways, and aquifers, combined with the reduction in evapotranspiration resulting from forest felling, is undermining aquatic biodiversity, degrading native soils, and causing unprecedented fluctuations in the moisture and rainfall cycles essential to multispecies flourishing across the Cerrado, the Amazon, and well beyond (Rekow 2019).
zh: 在巴西，大豆种植园集中于生态敏感地区，例如亚马孙地区：其大规模种植面积，从2006年的114万公顷增加到2016年的448万公顷，增长至约四倍；又如塞拉多地区，这里拥有世界上生物多样性最为丰富的一些热带稀树草原景观（Sauer 2018；Schneider et al. 2021）。与亚马孙不同，塞拉多位于2006年“大豆禁伐协议”的保护区域之外；这项自愿协议，旨在减少大豆生产直接造成的毁林（Brandão, Cardoso & Garrett 2025）。过去二十年间，单一种植开发使该地区损失了50%的原生植被，导致鬃狼、大食蚁兽、蓝眼地鸠和白鼻僧面猴等数以千计的特有动植物处于极度濒危状态。与此同时，为种植大豆而清理土地的刀耕火种方式，降低了空气质量，增加了温室气体排放，也使破碎化森林越来越容易遭受火灾。农化品渗入河流、水道和含水层，再加上森林砍伐导致的蒸散量减少，正在削弱水生生物多样性、破坏原生土壤，并造成湿度与降雨循环的空前波动；这些循环，对塞拉多、亚马孙乃至远远超出这两个地区的多物种繁盛，都至关重要（Rekow 2019）。
body.review: “极度濒危”依本段描述性表达critical endangerment译出，不据此给列举的所有物种统一赋予IUCN的“极危（CR）”等级。Soy Moratorium在此译“大豆禁伐协议”，指与毁林相关的自愿采购约束，并非全面禁止大豆种植。

en: Often, oil palm and soy expansion intensify, rather than create, the threats of extinction faced by tropical flora and fauna because they unfold within a broader mosaic of extractive industries, past and present. These industries include other agribusiness ventures, but also mining, logging, and pulp and paper operations, and infrastructural developments such as roads, railways, artificial waterways, hydroelectric dams, and ports, which together compound the vulnerability of ecosystems that endangered species depend on to survive and thrive. In the case of soy in the Brazilian Amazon, for example, and despite policies instituted under the aforementioned Soy Moratorium, agribusiness developments continue to drive indirect deforestation by establishing themselves on former cattle ranches and grazing areas that are then forced to move further inland. Forest fragments left standing between developed zones tend to be small, sparse, and susceptible to adverse and cumulative edge effects. The lack of biotic corridors connecting these fragile ecological patches often contributes to undermining their ecosystemic viability, including by hindering species migration and dispersal, and pollination through biotic vectors.
zh: 油棕与大豆的扩张，往往是在加剧热带动植物已经面临的灭绝威胁，而非从无到有地创造这些威胁，因为它们发生于一个由过去及当下的攫取性产业交织而成的更广阔格局中。这些产业不仅包括其他农业企业，也包括采矿、伐木、纸浆与造纸业，以及道路、铁路、人工水道、水电大坝和港口等基础设施开发。它们共同加重了生态系统的脆弱性，而受威胁物种依靠这些生态系统生存、繁衍。例如，在巴西亚马孙地区的大豆产业中，尽管前述“大豆禁伐协议”建立了相关政策，农业企业开发仍通过占据昔日的养牛牧场和放牧区，迫使后者进一步向腹地迁移，继续间接推动毁林。开发区之间残留下来的森林片段，通常面积小、分布稀疏，容易受到不利且累积的边缘效应影响。这些脆弱的生态斑块缺乏相互连接的生物廊道，常常进一步削弱其生态系统维持自身的能力，包括阻碍物种迁徙与扩散，以及通过生物媒介进行的授粉。

en: The extinctions and endangerments generated by the ‘modular simplifications’ of biodiverse landscapes turned agribusiness monocrops often work hand in hand with ‘feral proliferations’ that are directly linked to the genetic homogenization of plantation ecosystems (Tsing, Mathews & Bubandt 2019). For while on the short term, monocultures might be advantageous in terms of control and productivity, on the long-term, they are more vulnerable to the stresses of disease than polycultures, their uniformity creating a favourable habitat for pests specialised in predating on the particular species cultivated.
zh: 生物多样性丰富的景观被改造成农业企业的单一种植区，这种“模块化简化”造成的灭绝与濒危，常常与“野化增殖”并行；后者直接关联于种植园生态系统在遗传上的同质化（Tsing, Mathews & Bubandt 2019）。因为，尽管单一种植在短期内可能有利于控制与提高生产率，从长远来看，它却比复合种植更容易受到疾病压力影响。其整齐划一的特征，为那些专门侵害特定栽培物种的害虫与病原体，创造了有利的栖息环境。

en: In Mexico, for instance, the intensification and technologization of coffee cultivation, combined with mass deforestation and a resulting increase in wind-borne spore travel, triggered a massive outbreak in 2012–2013 of coffee leaf rust, a disease caused by the fungus

, which threatened to devastate coffee production across Central America, the Caribbean, and Colombia (see Figure 3). This epidemic has heightened the likelihood of future and more frequent outbreaks, especially given that rust-resistant varieties are vulnerable to other fungal diseases, such as ojo de gallo, and that many are already showing signs of rust infection (Perfecto, Jiménez-Soto & Vandermeer 2019). The susceptibility of monocrops to parasitic activity also comes to the fore in Honduras, where the shift in banana’s role from agroecological shade plant to industrial cash crop, dominated by a single variety (the Gros Michel), led to the rampant spread of Panama Disease (mál de Panamá, mata muerta, or

), which became one of the most economically significant epidemics of the twentieth century (Soluri 2000, 2005). Dense plantings and the homogeneity of the dominant plant, combined with the development of plantation-supporting infrastructures including irrigation canals, drainage ditches, and railroads, all conspired to facilitate the pathogen’s spread across the country and beyond. In Liberia, meanwhile, land clearing and the destruction of native flora and fauna to make way for rubber plantations in the early twentieth century allowed opportunistic insects to thrive, with hugely harmful impacts not only on plantation operations but also on workers’ health, wellbeing, and safety (Mitman 2021). One such parasite was the biting black fly (
spp.), that found an ideal home in plantation waterway infrastructures, wind breaks, and shade and that preyed on the blood of rubber tappers. Another was the worm

, that found a vector both in black flies and in the bodies of the rubber sector’s imported labour force, and that became one of the leading causes of blindness in sub-Saharan Africa and other regions of the tropics.
zh: 例如，在墨西哥，咖啡种植的集约化与技术化，同大规模毁林，以及毁林导致的孢子随风传播增加相结合，在2012—2013年引发了大规模咖啡叶锈病暴发。这种由咖啡驼孢锈菌（Hemileia vastatrix）造成的疾病，威胁到整个中美洲、加勒比地区和哥伦比亚的咖啡生产（见图3）。这次疫情提高了未来更频繁暴发的可能性，尤其是因为抗锈病品种容易感染其他真菌病，如ojo de gallo，而且许多品种已出现锈病感染迹象（Perfecto, Jiménez-Soto & Vandermeer 2019）。单一种植对寄生生物活动的易感性，在洪都拉斯也十分突出：香蕉从农业生态体系中的遮阴植物，转变成以单一品种“大米七”（Gros Michel）为主导的工业经济作物后，巴拿马病（mál de Panamá、mata muerta，或Fusarium oxysporum f. cubense）迅速蔓延，成为20世纪经济影响最重大的病害流行之一（Soluri 2000, 2005）。密集种植、主导作物的同质性，再加上为种植园服务的灌溉渠、排水沟和铁路等基础设施的发展，共同促使病原体蔓延到全国乃至境外。与此同时，在利比里亚，20世纪初为橡胶种植园让路而开展的土地清理，以及对本土动植物的破坏，使机会型昆虫大量繁衍，不仅严重损害种植园运营，也危及工人的健康、福祉与安全（Mitman 2021）。其中一种寄生者，是叮咬吸血的蚋（Simulium属诸种）：它在种植园水道设施、防风林和阴凉处找到理想栖息地，吸食割胶工人的血液。另一种则是盘尾丝虫（Onchocerca volvulus）；它以蚋以及橡胶业输入劳动力的身体作为传播载体，并成为撒哈拉以南非洲及其他热带地区失明的主要原因之一。
body.review: 底本将病名与病原名称并列，英文照录；其中Fusarium oxysporum f. cubense是病原真菌的名称，不是疾病本身的同义名称。关于河盲症，WHO说明由感染的蚋叮咬传播盘尾丝虫；人体是宿主与感染来源，不能把这里的vector一律理解成与蚋相同的生物媒介。

en: When it comes to cash crops like soy and oil palm, alongside jatropha, sugarcane, sugarbeet, sunflower, rapeseed, and corn, the great irony underlying multispecies extinctions, ecological destructions, and feral proliferations is that plantation expansion (together with associated deforestation and habitat degradation) is often driven by imperatives and discourses of sustainability, which are themselves in turn propelled by the urgency of transitioning from fossil fuel economies to renewable energy sources (Dauvergne & Neville 2010). Debates rage on within policy and scientific circles as to whether biofuel production calls for plantation expansion over greater areas of land or production intensification over limited territories (Byerlee, Stevenson & Villoria 2014). Proponents of the former argue that expansion helps diminish plantations’ ecological and ecosystemic impacts by distributing them out across larger geographies. Proponents of the latter, on the other hand, posit that intensification helps concentrate these impacts in more localized and controlled zones. Similarly, emerging progressive policies such as the Soy Moratorium have, on the one hand, been praised for supporting the preservation of exceptionally biodiverse ecosystems, and, on the other hand, criticized for legitimizing the transformation of biomes lying
regulations’ protective ambit into ‘sacrifice zones’ that are consequently rendered prone to heightened and ill-regulated exploitation (Oliveira & Hecht 2016).
zh: 在大豆和油棕，以及麻疯树、甘蔗、甜菜、向日葵、油菜与玉米等经济作物的情形中，多物种灭绝、生态破坏与野化增殖背后，有一种巨大的讽刺：推动种植园扩张及相应毁林、栖息地退化的，往往恰恰是可持续性的要求与话语；而推动这些要求和话语的，又是从化石燃料经济转向可再生能源的紧迫性（Dauvergne & Neville 2010）。政策界与科学界仍在激烈争论：生产生物燃料，究竟需要把种植园扩张到更大的土地范围，还是需要在有限地域内强化生产（Byerlee, Stevenson & Villoria 2014）。前一种立场的支持者认为，扩张可使种植园的生态与生态系统影响分散到更广阔的地理范围，从而减轻影响；后一种立场的支持者则认为，集约化有助于把这些影响集中在更局部、更可控的区域。类似地，“大豆禁伐协议”等新兴进步政策，一方面因有助于保护生物多样性极为丰富的生态系统而受到赞扬；另一方面，也因赋予某些转化过程以正当性而遭到批评：处于规制保护范围之外的生物群系，被变成“牺牲区”，因而更容易遭受加剧且监管不足的开发（Oliveira & Hecht 2016）。

en: The actual implementation and on-the-ground effectiveness of such policies and initiatives, meanwhile, can all too quickly be undermined or overturned as government priorities and global markets shift. In Brazil, a 2019 decree passed by then-President of Brazil, Jair Bolsonaro, lifted a ten-year ban on sugarcane cultivation in the Amazon rainforest and the Pantanal (the largest floodplain in the world and a UNESCO World Natural Heritage Site), thus legitimating agribusiness developments in an already highly vulnerable ecosystem (Lima et al. 2020). In Indonesia, a statement by newly elected President Prabowo Subianto in early 2025 called for the massive expansion of oil palm plantations to feed domestic food and biofuel demands, signalling the potential reversal of a moratorium initiated in 2011 on the issuance of new oil palm plantation permits and licences (Suhardi 2025). In these and many other instances, we see that efforts on paper and in practice to protect biodiversity within the plantation nexus are never set in stone, nor guaranteed to survive the volatile flux of shifting (geo)political climates, currents, and concerns.
zh: 与此同时，随着政府优先事项和全球市场发生变化，这类政策与倡议的实际实施及其在当地的成效，很容易迅速受到削弱，甚至被推翻。在巴西，时任总统雅伊尔·博索纳罗于2019年通过的一项法令，取消了在亚马孙雨林和潘塔纳尔地区种植甘蔗的十年禁令。潘塔纳尔是世界最大的洪泛平原，也是联合国教科文组织世界自然遗产地；这一法令，为在本已高度脆弱的生态系统中开展农业企业开发赋予了正当性（Lima et al. 2020）。在印度尼西亚，新当选总统普拉博沃·苏比延多于2025年初发表声明，呼吁大规模扩张油棕种植园，以满足国内食物和生物燃料需求。这表明，一项始于2011年、暂停发放新油棕种植园许可与执照的禁令，可能被逆转（Suhardi 2025）。这些以及其他许多事例表明，围绕种植园体系保护生物多样性的纸面和实践努力，从来不是一成不变的，也无法保证能够经受住不断变换的地缘政治及政治气候、潮流与关切。
body.review: 此处按作者叙述的2019年及2025年历史情境翻译；不将其当作当前总统任期、法律效力或许可状态说明。印度尼西亚2011年森林／泥炭地许可暂停与油棕专项许可政策的范围和沿革，尚需对照具体法令核验。

en: 3.2 Multispecies Lifeworlds and Histories
zh: 3.2　多物种生活世界与历史

en: The ecological destructions and disfigurations described in the previous section are inflected by local experiences, knowledges, and imaginaries that speak in different ways to how plantation developments reconfigure multispecies relations and lifeworlds, alongside biocultural histories and landscapes. What emerges from attending to these local onto-epistemologies is a bottom-up, nuanced understanding and appreciation of the deepentanglements of humanand non-human fates and futures in the face of monocrop expansion – entanglements that challenge assumptions of a neat divide between nature and culture in the context of anthropogenic formations like monocrop plantations.
zh: 上一节描述的生态破坏与变形，受到当地经验、知识和想象的折射；这些经验、知识与想象以不同方式，讲述种植园开发如何重塑多物种关系与生活世界，以及生物—文化历史和景观。关注这些地方性的本体论—认识论，会使我们自下而上地、细致地理解并体认：面对单一作物扩张，人类与非人的命运和未来，是何等深深纠缠在一起。这种纠缠挑战了如下假定：在单一作物种植园这类人为形成的体系中，自然与文化之间存在着清晰的界线。
body.review: 底本此段将deep entanglements与human and分别紧连为deepentanglements、humanand，英文照录；中文按句意分读。

en: The terrains of Central Italy offer a compelling example of such entanglements and their layered, temporal dimensions. Here, local inhabitants read in the textures and terrains of the landscape multiple intertwined histories of changing multispecies interactions and inheritances – from the destruction of chestnut orchards that their families cultivated and managed for hundreds of years by pathogens introduced through international trade in the mid-nineteenth to mid-twentieth centuries, to the expansion of state-driven pine plantations in the context of rapid capitalist expansion in the early nineteenth century, which transformed rural peasants and shepherds into industrial workers (Mathews 2018). As they walk, notice, draw, and describe the landscape, local farmers and foresters identify in the morphology of trees the traces of their prior relationships with humans, diseases, fires, and soils, and connect these in their discourses to history, politics, state-making, and broader processes of environmental change. They mourn the enforced abandonment of traditional crop varieties, together with the loss of related practices, including litter raking and controlled burning, that accompanied the rise of conifer concessions. They express deep concern over the dramatic increase of fires resulting from the expansion of the fire-prone species

. At the same time, they draw on multispecies histories embedded in the landscape to envision and enact other kinds of futures for themselves and their non-human companions – from efforts to preserve low-elevation chestnut varieties that are more resilient to climate change, to initiatives to support the livelihoods of formerly displaced and ongoingly precarious peasant firewood cutters.
zh: 意大利中部的土地，为这种纠缠及其层叠的时间维度提供了一个有力例证。在这里，当地居民从景观的纹理与地貌中，读出多条相互缠绕的历史：多物种互动与传承如何不断变化——从19世纪中叶至20世纪中叶，经由国际贸易传入的病原体，摧毁了他们家族栽培和管理数百年的栗园；到19世纪初资本主义迅速扩张背景下，国家推动的松树种植园不断蔓延，把乡村农民与牧羊人变成产业工人（Mathews 2018）。当地农民与林业工作者一边行走、观察、绘画和描述景观，一边在树木的形态中辨认出它们此前与人类、疾病、火灾及土壤发生关系的痕迹，并在讲述中把这些痕迹同历史、政治、国家建构及更广泛的环境变化过程联系起来。他们哀叹，被迫放弃传统作物品种，也失去了耙集落叶和控制性燃烧等相关实践；这些丧失伴随着针叶林特许经营区的兴起。他们对易燃树种海岸松（Pino marittimo）的扩张所造成的火灾激增，深感忧虑。与此同时，他们借助嵌入景观的多物种历史，为自己及非人伙伴设想并实现别样的未来——从努力保护更能适应气候变化的低海拔栗树品种，到发起行动，支持那些昔日遭到驱离、至今生计仍不稳定的农民伐薪者。

en: Intertwined histories of more-than-human violence and vulnerability are also at play in the Argentinian Gran Chaco, where large-scale soy fields are being developed today upon landscapes formerly occupied by sugarcane monocrops (Gordillo 2004, 2014). Indigenous communities including the Toba People connect these consecutive histories of plantation proliferation to a range of material, ecological, and affective ruptures that have over time severed them from their intimate and ancestral relations to the landscape, and that materialize not only in soy fields but also in the rubble and debris of colonial infrastructures that were tethered to the plantation project: lost cities, abandoned train stations, Catholic missions, Spanish fortresses, mass graves, and destroyed forests. The substitution of sugar with soy, too, conjures and multiplies traumatic memories among local workers of the nefarious, supernatural entities who are said to make plantations their abode, including devils, cannibals, and sorcerers who fed off the flesh of labourers, estranged them from their territories, plagued them with disease, and created a general atmosphere of death and of terror (see also Lattas 1993). Such memories are contrasted by the Toba to the ecologies that plantations replace, and particularly the Chaco bush, which is associated with health, healing, and resilience, and with devils that, unlike those inhabiting monocrops, have long entertained reciprocal and life-sustaining relations with humans as guardians and companions.
zh: 在人类之外同样展开的暴力与脆弱性交织而成的历史，也存在于阿根廷大查科地区。如今，人们正在昔日被甘蔗单一种植占据的景观上，开发大规模豆田（Gordillo 2004, 2014）。包括托巴人在内的原住民社群，把种植园先后扩散的这些历史，同一系列物质、生态与情感上的断裂联系起来。随着时间推移，这些断裂切断了他们与景观之间亲密且源自祖先的关系；其物质表现不仅见于豆田，也见于那些曾依附种植园计划的殖民基础设施的残垣碎片：消失的城镇、废弃的火车站、天主教传教站、西班牙堡垒、万人坑和遭到摧毁的森林。大豆取代甘蔗，也唤起并增殖了当地工人的创伤记忆：据说，有些邪恶的超自然存在栖居在种植园，其中有魔鬼、食人者和巫师；它们以劳动者的血肉为食，使他们与自己的土地疏离，以疾病折磨他们，营造出笼罩一切的死亡与恐怖氛围（另见Lattas 1993）。托巴人把这些记忆，同被种植园替代的生态世界相对照，尤其是查科灌木林。后者意味着健康、疗愈与韧性，也同魔鬼相联系；但这些魔鬼不同于栖居单一种植区的那些，长期以来，它们作为守护者和伙伴，与人类维持着互惠并滋养生命的关系。

en: The more-than-human distribution of plantation-driven disease, death, and violence constitutes a central motif not only in ethnographic accounts of monocrop lifeworlds but also in literary works, representations, and critiques. Particularly prominent here is the vast corpus of literature stemming from the Caribbean, a region whose history, culture, politics, ecology, and economy have been profoundly shaped by the territory-claiming nature of colonial sugarcane plantations (Benítez-Rojo 1996; Trouillot 2002; Loichot 2013; Hiddleston 2025). For instance, stories and poems authored by Martinican author, poet, and founder of the Négritude movement in Francophone literature, Aimé Césaire (2001), convey a disturbing confusion between human bodies and plantation machinery, with landscapes transformed by intensive industrialization bearing the same physical marks of disease, torture, suffering, starvation, and attrition as the flesh of the labourers forced to sustain them with their blood and their sweat, and that of the environments and species sacrificed in plantations’ wake. Similarly, the Martinican novelist and pioneer of the créolité movement, Patrick Chamoiseau (1994), writes of Black workers’ bodies mirroring the disposability of landscapes depleted and disfigured to make way for sugarcane. In his vivid descriptions, the mouths of the starved lead them to the cannibalistic mouth of plantations as forest-demolishing, crop-displacing, and labour-sucking machines that swallow the famished whole – like the mouth of the inferno. In both instances, uncanny resonances arise between the rampant ecological defacements produced by plantation proliferation and the facelessness of enslaved Black people themselves, as fungible matter deemed sub-human under rapacious White imperial-capitalist regimes.
zh: 种植园造成的疾病、死亡与暴力在跨越人类边界的生命之间分布，不仅是单一种植生活世界民族志叙述的核心主题，也是文学作品、再现与批判的重要主题。在这方面，尤为突出的是加勒比地区的浩繁文学。殖民甘蔗种植园攫占领土的特性，深刻塑造了这个地区的历史、文化、政治、生态与经济（Benítez-Rojo 1996；Trouillot 2002；Loichot 2013；Hiddleston 2025）。例如，马提尼克作家、诗人、法语文学“黑人性”（Négritude）运动创始人艾梅·塞泽尔（Aimé Césaire 2001）所写的故事与诗歌，传达出人类身体与种植园机器之间令人不安的混同。被密集工业化改造的景观，同那些被迫以血汗供养种植园的劳动者的肉身，以及被种植园牺牲的环境与物种一样，都带有疾病、酷刑、苦难、饥饿和耗损的身体印记。同样，马提尼克小说家、“克里奥尔性”（créolité）运动先驱帕特里克·夏穆瓦索（Patrick Chamoiseau 1994）写道，黑人工人的身体，映照着那些为了给甘蔗让路而耗竭、变形的景观同样可被抛弃的处境。在他生动的描述中，饥民的嘴巴把他们引向种植园那张食人的大嘴：种植园是毁灭森林、挤走作物、吸榨劳动的机器，将饥饿者囫囵吞下——犹如地狱之口。在这两个例子中，种植园扩散所造成的猖獗的生态毁容，与被奴役黑人自身被剥去面孔的处境，产生了诡异的共鸣：在贪婪的白人帝国—资本主义体制下，他们被视为低于人的、可以相互替换的物质。

en: Indigenous responses to oil palm expansion across the tropics further communicate the cultural, spiritual, and affective significance of radical ecosystemic shifts resulting from the conversion of biodiverse forests to monocrop plantations. In the Bajo Atrato region of Colombia, for example, forest clearing to make way for oil palm developments is associated by Indigenous and Afro-Colombian communities with an unprecedented explosion in poisonous snake populations, whose bites are notoriously difficult to treat with herbal medicines normally used by traditional curers, and whose threat to human bodies is understood to result from the contamination of the landscape by oil palm (Ruiz-Serna 2023). The plantation-driven proliferation of lethal creatures such as snakes is compounded by a growing scarcity of native game animals, which communities interpret as symptomatic of a breakdown in relations of respect, reverence, and reciprocity with protective spirit masters who are angered by the relentless deforestation unfolding across the land and threatening native animals. In both instances, damage to the territory as a victim of violence works hand in hand with damage to ecosystems and human and non-human bodies, the collective healing of which is at once urgent and inchoate.
zh: 原住民对热带各地油棕扩张的回应，进一步传达出：生物多样性丰富的森林变成单一作物种植园，由此引发的剧烈生态系统变化，有着文化、精神与情感上的意义。例如，在哥伦比亚阿特拉托河下游地区，原住民和非裔哥伦比亚人社群，把为油棕开发而清林，同毒蛇数量空前激增联系起来。被这些蛇咬伤后，传统治疗者惯用的草药很难奏效；人们认为，毒蛇对人体的威胁，源于油棕对景观的污染（Ruiz-Serna 2023）。种植园驱动的蛇类等致命生物的增殖，又与本土猎物日益稀少相叠加。当地社群将后者解读为：他们与具有护佑作用的灵界主宰之间，尊重、敬畏和互惠的关系已经破裂；这些灵界主宰被遍及大地、威胁本土动物的无休止毁林激怒了。在这两种情形中，作为暴力受害者的领土所遭到的伤害，与生态系统、人类及非人身体受到的伤害相伴而生；对它们的共同疗愈既十分迫切，又仍未成形。

en: In Southeast Asia, where oil palm was first cultivated in the form of large-scale monocrops, Indigenous communities often associate plantation developments with experiences of loss, estrangement, regret, longing, and absence that crystallize in affective and cultural terms how ecological declines and disappearances intersect with human wellbeing. Among the Batek of Peninsular Malaysia, for instance, the obliteration of traditionally cultivated and harvested native forest fruits, tubers, and shoots conjures what the Batek call haʔip, or a deep feeling of yearning, love, and nostalgia for the forest’s now-ruptured cycles of growth, senescence, and rebirth, and the erasure of nourishing multispecies pasts once embedded in the living landscape (Rudge 2024). The deeply sensory dimensions of haʔip are conveyed in prevalent local characterizations of plantation extinctions through the landscape’s changing smells, sights, and sounds: the red sticky substances that indicate blood and death, the unfamiliar screaming of invisible ghosts, and the unpleasant scents of decay that stunt the ripening of fruits. Lived in and through the immediacy of the body, haʔip also takes on an anticipatory or speculative dimension, as people envision or predict potential losses in the future, wherein remaining patches of forest may no longer exist nor be able to offer refuge, sustenance, memories, and knowledges to Batek generations to come.
zh: 在东南亚——油棕最早以大规模单一作物形式栽培的地区——原住民社群常把种植园开发同丧失、疏离、遗憾、思念与缺席的经验联系起来。这些经验，在情感与文化层面，凝结了生态衰退、消失与人类福祉相交织的方式。例如，在马来半岛的巴特克人中，传统上栽培与采集的本土森林果实、块茎及嫩芽的消失，唤起了他们所说的haʔip：对森林如今已被打断的生长、衰老与再生循环，怀有深切的渴望、爱恋与怀念，也哀惜那些曾嵌入活的景观、滋养生命的多物种往昔遭到抹除（Rudge 2024）。当地人常通过景观中气味、景象与声音的变化来描述种植园造成的灭绝，传达出haʔip深刻的感官维度：意味着鲜血与死亡的红色黏稠物质、看不见的幽灵发出的陌生尖叫，以及阻碍果实成熟的难闻腐败气味。haʔip在人们即时的身体经验之中、也通过身体被感受，同时还具有预期或推想的维度：人们想象或预测未来可能发生的丧失，届时，残存的森林斑块也许将不复存在，无法再为后来的巴特克世代提供庇护、食物、记忆和知识。

en: In West Papua, where over one million hectares of forest have been razed for oil palm in the last decade, Marind communities with whom I work describe ecological loss and destruction as producing a form of spatiotemporal and bodily alienation that is experienced by humans and non-humans alike (Chao 2024). This alienation manifests in people’s incapacity to recognize, relate to, and orient themselves against the regimented uniformity of agribusiness landscapes that are stripped of all spatial and temporal markers, in the disturbing stillness of monocrops as spaces of loneliness and solitude, and in the violent substitution of lively forest bioacoustics with deathly plantation sonics, as singing birds, chirruping insects, and grunting cassowaries give way to roaring bulldozers, gnawing chainsaws, and rumbling trucks. Like the Batek, Marind associate plantation developments with the severance of intimate relations with kindred native plants and animals (amai) that they share common descent with from ancestral spirits (dema) and after whom their clans are named. They also speak of plantations as erasing the spatially embedded past by destroying the sacred sites that were created by ancestral spirits in time immemorial, polluting the patterned bark of sago palms wherein past droughts and fires are imprinted, and depleting populations of wild boars and cassowaries in whose fur and feathers once shimmered the memories of human and more-than-human relatives, both living and deceased (Chao 2022a; Chao 2024). By imposing their mono-time of homogeneous growth on the formerly polytemporal rhythms and overlapping histories of the forest, plantations, as spaces of alienation and disconnection, produce for Marind an out-of-joint present – one whose literal and figurative horizonlessness thwarts the possibility of imagining and enacting meaningful, multispecies futures.
zh: 在西巴布亚，过去十年间，超过一百万公顷森林被夷平，用来种植油棕。与我合作的马林德社群将生态丧失与破坏描述为一种时空及身体的异化，人类与非人共同经历着这种异化（Chao 2024）。它表现为：面对剥除了所有时空标记、整齐划一的农业企业景观，人们无法辨认、建立关系或确定自身方位；作为孤独与寂寞空间的单一种植区，呈现出令人不安的静止；生机勃勃的森林生命声响，被死气沉沉的种植园声响暴力取代——鸣唱的鸟、唧唧的昆虫和低鸣的食火鸡，让位于咆哮的推土机、啃噬般作响的链锯及隆隆的卡车。与巴特克人一样，马林德人把种植园开发，同他们与本土亲属植物和动物（amai）之间亲密关系的断裂联系起来。他们与这些动植物共同源于祖灵（dema），各氏族也以其命名。他们还说，种植园毁坏祖灵在远古创造的圣地，污染记录着昔日干旱与火灾印记的西谷椰树斑纹树皮，并使野猪和食火鸡种群衰减，从而抹除了嵌入空间的过去；曾经，野猪的毛与食火鸡的羽翎中，闪烁着关于健在及逝去的人类和超越人类亲属的记忆（Chao 2022a；Chao 2024）。种植园作为异化与断联的空间，把自身同质生长的单一时间，强加于森林原先具有多重时间的节律和交叠历史，为马林德人制造了一个脱节的当下：在字面与隐喻意义上都没有地平线，也就阻断了想象和实现有意义的多物种未来的可能。

en: 3.3 Conservation and Sustainability
zh: 3.3　保护与可持续性

en: In recent years, growing awareness of the adverse ecological impacts of plantations – in large part driven by civil society protests within the broader context of the global climate crisis – has given rise to a spate of corporate and state initiatives intended to enhance the environmental sustainability of agribusiness projects. These include conservation areas established to offset the ecosystemic damages caused by monocultures, national parks created to protect critically endangered species, organic and fairtrade production systems, and Corporate Social Responsibility protocols, principles, and criteria that integrate socio-environmental concerns into business operations (Colchester, Chao & Jiwan 2012). However, conservation and sustainability initiatives, while arguably laudable in their intentions, are often designed and implemented by scientists, technocrats, and politicians without sufficient consideration for the complex social, historical, and spiritual relations that people on the ground entertain with local landscapes and their constitutive lifeforms.
zh: 近年来，人们日益认识到种植园的不利生态影响——在更广泛的全球气候危机背景下，这种认识在很大程度上由公民社会的抗议推动——由此涌现出一系列企业与国家倡议，旨在增强农业企业项目的环境可持续性。其中包括：为抵偿单一种植造成的生态系统损害而建立的保护区，为保护极危物种而设立的国家公园，有机与公平贸易生产体系，以及将社会—环境关切纳入企业经营的“企业社会责任”规程、原则和标准（Colchester, Chao & Jiwan 2012）。然而，保护与可持续性倡议的意图虽可称许，其设计和实施却常由科学家、技术官僚及政治人物主导，未能充分考虑当地人同地方景观及构成这些景观的生命形式之间，复杂的社会、历史与精神关系。

en: Take the case of elephant conservation in the northeastern Indian state of Assam, home to the country’s largest area of tea plantations and the source of over half of national tea production. Assamese landscapes are shared through intimate and fraught relations of co-presence between humans and elephants, who are worshipped as powerful gods but also feared for their regular and, at times, lethal attacks on human settlements and agriculture (Keil 2025). Far from benign, human-elephant entanglements involve an ongoingly negotiated exchange of needs, mobilities, and survival that is rife with interspecies tension, vulnerability, and friction (Münster 2014). Such tensions are now exacerbated by the state-endorsed establishment of wildlife corridors as a corrective to the habitat fragmentation resulting from deforestation, tea planting, and associated infrastructural developments (Barua 2024).
zh: 以印度东北部阿萨姆邦的大象保护为例。这里拥有全国面积最大的茶园，茶产量占全国一半以上。人类与大象通过亲密却充满矛盾的共在关系，共享阿萨姆的景观：大象被奉为强大的神灵，但它们经常袭击人类聚落与农田，有时甚至致人死亡，也因而令人畏惧（Keil 2025）。人与象的纠缠远非温和无害，而是涉及需求、移动与生存之间持续协商的交换，充满物种间的紧张、脆弱性与摩擦（Münster 2014）。如今，为补救毁林、植茶及相关基础设施开发造成的栖息地破碎化，国家支持建立野生动物廊道，反而加剧了这些紧张（Barua 2024）。

en: Exemplifying a new model of conservation anchored in principles of landscape connectivity and flow rather than rigid spatial enclosure, wildlife corridors seek to prevent the isolation of herds and thus improve the genetic variability of overall species populations. On the ground, however, the designation of strips of land as ecological corridors has placed growing pressure on farmers to hand over their land and given rise to grassroots protests that stem from radically different understandings of the factors shaping the mobility of elephants. Many local inhabitants, for instance, see themselves, and not the state or conservation scientists, as the guardians of wildlife. They have, since time immemorial, learned to create safe passages for elephants yet are now labelled as encroachers and face eviction from their ancestral lands in the name of conservation. These communities also emphasize that, in contrast to schematic mappings of animal mobility, elephants are highly non-linear in their patterns of movement across the landscape, taking different trajectories in the manner of interlacing trails rather than unidirectional lines. The planned conversion of tea plantations into wildlife conservation habitats poses a particular threat to Adivasi communities, whose ability to transition to other livelihoods is undermined by their status as marginalized Indigenous Peoples and landless workers. As a result, connectivity conservation, intended to limit the environmental damages of plantation proliferation, may very well transform into yet another strategy for expanding state-corporate governance over land and life – one that furthers, in an ecological guise, rather than challenges, the uneven human and more-than-human biopolitics of plantation logics (Barua 2024).
zh: 野生动物廊道体现了一种新的保护模式，其基础是景观连通与流动的原则，而非僵硬的空间封闭。它力图防止象群彼此孤立，从而提高整个物种种群的遗传变异性。然而，在当地，把条带状土地划为生态廊道，使农民交出土地的压力日益增大，也引发了基层抗议；抗议源于人们对塑造大象移动性的因素有着根本不同的理解。例如，许多当地居民认为，自己才是野生动物的守护者，而非国家或保护科学家。自远古以来，他们便学会了为大象创造安全通道，如今却被贴上侵占者的标签，面临以保护之名被逐出祖地的处境。这些社群还强调，与动物移动的示意地图不同，大象在景观中的活动方式高度非线性，沿不同路径行进，形成的是交织的小径，而非单向直线。把茶园转为野生动物保护栖息地的计划，对阿迪瓦西社群构成特别严重的威胁；作为边缘化原住民族和无地劳动者的地位，削弱了他们转向其他生计的能力。因此，旨在限制种植园扩散所造成的环境损害的连通性保护，完全可能转变为国家—企业扩张其对土地与生命治理的另一种策略：它披着生态外衣，推进而非挑战种植园逻辑中不平等的人类及超越人类的生命政治（Barua 2024）。

en: In the neighbouring Indian state of West Bengal, home to the tea-growing city of Darjeeling, the ways in which local workers experience and articulate the transition from chemically sustained monocultures to organic and polycultural tea cultivation speak in a different way to the ambiguous or double-edged effects of visions of environmental sustainability, or Green Growth (Kumpf 2024). On the one hand, this transition has enlivened the landscape through the resurgence of myriad lifeforms that are finding new fodder and futures in organic tea plantations – from bugs and fungi to owls, hornbills, and tigers. Encounters with these organisms are a source of wonder, surprise, pleasure, curiosity, and much-welcome distraction for plantation workers, their sensory and affective valences helping to interrupt the monotony and repetitiveness of tea plucking. Of particular significance within this emergent ecology is the tea leaf insect, or tea deva in local parlance, which mimics the shape of tea leaves and has returned to the plantations since pesticide use was abolished. Tea devas are venerated as cherished deities, valued as emblems of ecological renewal, and interpreted as evidence of harmonious landscape dynamics. At the same time, however, their sanctioned protection, along with that of other re-emerging lifeforms, has become yet another (often under-compensated) task imposed upon the daily routine of precarious workers who themselves remain economically marginalized and subject to exploitative labour conditions that have changed little, if at all, since the colonial period (Sen 2017). Experiences of wonder and pleasure work hand in hand with realities of exhaustion, disempowerment, and frustration, as a valued species become elevated to an extra-human position in the name of sustainability, but at the cost of the wellbeing of human labourers who remain relegated to the lowest rung of the plantation hierarchy.
zh: 在毗邻的印度西孟加拉邦——产茶城市大吉岭所在地——当地工人对从化学投入维持的单一种植，转向有机、复合茶叶栽培的经历与表述，以另一种方式揭示了环境可持续性或“绿色增长”愿景含混且双刃的效应（Kumpf 2024）。一方面，这一转型使景观焕发生机，无数生命形式重新出现，在有机茶园中找到新的食物与未来：从昆虫和真菌，到猫头鹰、犀鸟与老虎。与这些生物的相遇，为种植园工人带来惊奇、意外、愉悦、好奇，以及求之不得的分心时刻；它们的感官与情感意义，有助于打破采茶劳动的单调重复。在这个涌现的生态世界中，尤其重要的是茶叶虫，当地称为tea deva。它模拟茶叶的形状，自农药停用后便返回茶园。茶叶虫被奉为珍爱的神灵，视为生态更新的象征，也被解读为景观动态和谐的证据。然而，与此同时，获得正式认可的茶叶虫保护，以及其他重新出现的生命形式的保护，又成为强加给处境不稳的工人的一项日常任务，而且往往补偿不足。这些工人自身仍在经济上遭到边缘化，并承受着自殖民时期以来几乎没有改变的剥削性劳动条件（Sen 2017）。惊奇与愉悦的经验，同疲惫、无权与挫折的现实并存：一个受到珍视的物种，以可持续性之名，被抬升到高于人的地位，代价却是那些仍被压在种植园等级制度底层的人类劳动者的福祉。

en: Conservation schemes to protect the critically endangered orangutan in Indonesian Borneo offer a distinctive yet complementary lens into the challenges of achieving ecological sustainability when it is at odds with local ways of knowing and relating across species lines. An iconic mascot in anti-deforestation and anti-plantation campaigns worldwide, there is perhaps no animal that captures the plight of critically endangered species better than the orangutan. Wild populations on the islands of Borneo and Sumatra have more than halved as a result of deforestation and fires caused by oil palm plantations as well as poaching and illegal wildlife trafficking. The species’ slow reproduction rates only exacerbate their risk of extinction, which is predicted to occur within the next ten to twenty years (Meijaard et al. 2011, 2018).
zh: 印度尼西亚婆罗洲旨在保护极危猩猩的计划，为理解如下挑战提供了一个独特而互补的视角：当生态可持续性同地方上跨越物种界线的认识方式和关系方式相抵触时，如何实现它？猩猩是全球反毁林、反种植园运动的标志性形象；也许没有哪种动物，比它更能体现极危物种的困境。由于油棕种植园导致的毁林与火灾，以及偷猎和非法野生动物贸易，婆罗洲与苏门答腊岛上的野生猩猩种群已经减少了一半以上。猩猩繁殖速度缓慢，只会进一步加剧灭绝风险；据预测，它们将在未来十至二十年内灭绝（Meijaard et al. 2011, 2018）。
body.review: “未来十至二十年内灭绝”是底本援引2011年和2018年文献作出的表述，按作者原文保留；不应把它改作从译稿制作之日开始计算的预测，也不表示已核实这一预测适用于所有野生猩猩种群。

en: On the ground, however, internationally funded conservation schemes, including orangutan rescue, rehabilitation, and adoption programs, are often critiqued by local inhabitants, to whom promises of material gain from various development projects, including oil palm plantations, have yet to materialize, and who still do not enjoy basic facilities such as electricity, running water, health care, and communications. For these economically precarious communities, the vast sums of money, as well as time and effort, invested in salvaging and relocating orangutans and then training them to survive in the wild are a source of bafflement and consternation, as well as sentiments of injustice in a world where, as one villager puts it, ‘only the orangutans get a life jacket’ (Chua et al. 2021: 370). Some express concerns over the potential risks posed by the planned introduction and release of orangutans to their rice paddy fields, which represent their primary source of subsistence. Many see wildlife conservation projects as yet another manifestation of ongoing asymmetries in power between global and local actors, long-standing conflicts over ownership and responsibility, the marginalization of Indigenous communities and voices, and the erasure of customary rights, or adat.
zh: 然而在当地，猩猩救援、康复与认养等国际资助的保护计划，常遭到居民批评。包括油棕种植园在内的各种开发项目，向他们许诺的物质收益尚未兑现；他们仍无法享有电力、自来水、医疗和通信等基本设施。对这些经济处境不稳的社群而言，耗费巨资、时间与精力，抢救和迁移猩猩，再训练其在野外生存，令人困惑、震惊，并引发不公正感；在这样的世界中，正如一位村民所言，“只有猩猩能得到救生衣”（Chua et al. 2021: 370）。一些人担心，计划引入并放归的猩猩，可能危及他们赖以为生的主要来源——稻田。许多人认为，野生动物保护项目，不过是下列持续现象的又一种体现：全球与地方行动者之间的权力不对等，围绕所有权和责任的长期冲突，原住民社群及其声音被边缘化，以及习惯权利（adat）遭到抹除。

en: While orangutans share historical and mythical connections to humans alongside other species such as snakes, crocodiles, and hornbills, they are not deemed by communities to be particularly special, nor are they prioritized within local cosmologies. Often, in fact, orangutans are not described by communities as vulnerable victims but rather as agentive entities who are responsible for their own actions (including, importantly, being rightfully killed if posing a life-threat to humans), and who are traditionally associated with mutual avoidance and antagonism, rather than cultivated proximity or intimacy. These local understandings differ markedly from the global representation of orangutans as a charismatic species, capable of attracting compassion, empathy, and action on the part of their all-too-resemblant human cousins. They form the grounds for grassroots critiques of conservation projects that are intended to protect endangered species but that, in the process, exacerbate socio-economic injustices for local inhabitants and impose upon them a duty to care for wildlife that contravenes local notions of multispecies agency, relationality, and responsibility.
zh: 虽然猩猩同蛇、鳄鱼和犀鸟等其他物种一样，与人类存在历史和神话上的联系，但当地社群并不认为它们特别特殊，也不在本地宇宙观中赋予其优先地位。事实上，社群往往并不把猩猩描述为脆弱的受害者，而把它们视为具有能动性、应为自身行动负责的存在——特别包括：若它们威胁人的生命，杀死它们便被认为正当。传统上，人猩关系的特征是彼此回避与敌对，而不是主动培养接近或亲密。这些地方理解，与全球层面对猩猩的再现显著不同：后者把它们塑造成富有魅力的物种，能够吸引那些与它们如此相像的人类表亲的同情、共感和行动。这些地方理解构成了基层批评保护项目的基础：项目本意在于保护濒危物种，却在过程中加剧了当地居民所受的社会经济不公，并强加给他们照料野生动物的义务，而这种义务违反了地方上关于多物种能动性、关系性与责任的观念。

en: In the Papuan oil palm sector, another understanding of sustainability-driven environmental initiatives is at play. Implemented by agribusiness corporations as part of a commitment to responsible palm oil production under international certification standards such as the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil, these initiatives require that companies identify, demarcate, monitor, and enhance areas classified as ‘High Conservation Value’. This includes forests with high concentrations of rare, threatened, or endangered species, and areas that provide critical ecological services such as watershed protection and soil erosion control (Chao 2019). Yet, despite their purportedly beneficial value, conservation zones are a source of widespread frustration and sorrow for many Indigenous Marind communities. For starters, what distinguishes a high from a low conservation value zone is unclear. Plants and animals, Marind emphasize, depend upon diverse ecologies that are all equally important to their subsistence, reproduction, and growth – swamps, marshlands, mangroves, savannah, forest, and more. While non-humans are restricted to bounded zones of liveability, Marind themselves are now excluded from areas where they once hunted, foraged, and fished, as access to these areas is forbidden to all except company personnel, conservation scientists, and sustainability auditors. Reciprocal relations of care between diverse organisms are thwarted by a stratification-cum-dissection of space and species that runs counter to Marind’s characterization of the forest as a realm enlivened by the sympoietic interactions of humans and other-than-humans. In the process, the unjust exclusion of Indigenous communities from the ecologies that sustain them goes hand in hand with the unjust severance of sentient ecologies themselves from the humans who care for and maintain them.
zh: 在巴布亚的油棕产业中，对可持续性驱动的环境倡议，还存在另一种理解。农业企业按照“可持续棕榈油圆桌倡议”等国际认证标准，承诺以负责任的方式生产棕榈油，并把这些环境倡议作为履行承诺的一部分。这些倡议要求公司辨识、划定、监测并提升被归类为“高保护价值”的地区，包括稀有、受威胁或濒危物种高度集中的森林，以及提供流域保护、水土流失控制等关键生态服务的区域（Chao 2019）。然而，尽管保护区被宣称具有益处，它们却给许多马林德原住民社群带来普遍的挫折与悲伤。首先，高保护价值区与低保护价值区的区别并不明确。马林德人强调，植物和动物依靠多种生态环境维生、繁衍和成长，沼泽、湿地、红树林、稀树草原、森林等等，都同样重要。非人生命被限制在划定边界的可生存区域内；马林德人自己，也被排除在曾经狩猎、采集和捕鱼的地区之外，因为除公司人员、保护科学家及可持续性审核员之外，所有人都被禁止进入这些地区。对空间与物种进行分级兼切割，阻断了不同生物之间相互照料的关系，也违背了马林德人对森林的理解：森林是人类与非人通过共同生成的互动而赋予活力的领域。在这一过程中，不公正地把原住民社群排除出供养他们的生态世界，与不公正地将有感知能力的生态世界本身同照料、维系它们的人类分离，同时发生。

en: Species cut off from their relations to humans in the name of environmental conservation are a source of great sadness (kesedihan) for Marind. Most notable among these is the sago palm, a plant of central significance in Marind culture and the source of their staple starch, sago flour (Chao 2021c). In conservation zones, Marind cannot care for sago palms through traditional practices like trimming, selective felling, and transplanting that enhance sago’s access to sunlight and nutrients and render their environment more conducive to healthy growth. As selective transplanting cannot take place, palms in conservation zones tend to reproduce sexually rather than vegetatively. In contrast to vegetative reproduction, this ends the life cycle of the parent palm, whose seeds disperse across great distances and germinate far away from their sago kin. These seedlings tend to differ morphologically from their kin, unlike vegetatively propagated suckers that form clonal colonies of similar genetic makeup to their parent. They also exhibit a slower and less regular rate of growth. Separated from each other, sago seeds and their parents are said to become ‘dry’ (kering), ‘lonely’ (kesendirian), and ‘sad’ (sedih) – sentiments that are also experienced and described by Marind themselves as traditional sago carers. Meanwhile, the segregation of palms to conservation zones negates the possibility of creating shared memories and relations between people and plants. As Pius Gebze, a village elder and close friend, explained to me, ‘when sago and humans grow apart, they suffer because they no longer share skin or wetness. They can no longer make stories or futures together. This is the violence of conservation’.
zh: 以环境保护之名，被切断与人类关系的物种，令马林德人深感悲伤（kesedihan）。其中最突出的是西谷椰：它在马林德文化中具有核心意义，也是他们主食淀粉——西谷米粉——的来源（Chao 2021c）。在保护区内，马林德人无法通过修剪、选择性砍伐和移栽等传统实践照料西谷椰；这些实践能够让西谷椰获得更多阳光和养分，使环境更有利于健康生长。由于无法进行选择性移栽，保护区内的西谷椰往往以有性繁殖取代营养繁殖。与营养繁殖不同，这会结束母树的生命周期；其种子传播到很远的地方，远离西谷椰亲属萌发。这些实生苗在形态上往往不同于亲属；而通过营养繁殖长成的萌蘖，会形成遗传组成与母树相近的克隆群落。实生苗的生长也更慢、更不规律。据说，彼此分离的西谷椰种子与亲本会变得“干燥”（kering）、“孤独”（kesendirian）和“悲伤”（sedih）；作为传统西谷椰照料者的马林德人，也经历并描述这些感受。与此同时，把西谷椰隔离在保护区内，否定了人与植物创造共同记忆和关系的可能。正如村中长者、我的挚友皮乌斯·格布泽（Pius Gebze）向我解释的：“当西谷椰与人类逐渐分离时，他们会痛苦，因为他们不再共享皮肤或湿润。他们再也不能一起创造故事或未来。这就是保护的暴力。”

en: 3.4 Conclusions
zh: 3.4　结论

en: The material presented in this section uncovers how plantations are grounded both in the necropolitics of a ‘hegemonic, extinction-oriented creed’ (Tsing 2011: 19) and in an instrumental biopolitics that requires that anything

supportive of cash crop liveliness and lucrativeness either die or be displaced (Hetherington 2019; Besky 2020). The monocultural logic undergirding these conjoined processes, as Indian activist and scholar Vandana Shiva (1993) critiques, is intolerant of alternative systems of cultivation or knowledge, and primarily economistic and anti-pluralistic in its telos. This intolerance includes a common disregard for long-standing Indigenous and local ways of relating to the environment and its more-than-human dwellers, and for the culturally and spiritually shaped ways in which people on the ground experience, interpret, and engage with rapidly transforming landscapes (Kröger 2022). It also comes tethered to an epistemic myopia regarding the ability of non-human life to exert its own influences and effects over and against human-driven projects, as exemplified by the activities of pests, parasites, and other feral organisms who repurpose capitalist natures as homes and hosts (Tomich 2011; Ovstehage 2021).
zh: 本部分呈现的材料揭示了，种植园同时奠基于两种政治：一种是“霸权性的、以灭绝为导向的信条”所体现的死亡政治（Tsing 2011: 19）；另一种是工具性的生命政治，它要求任何不利于经济作物的生机和获利能力的事物，要么死亡，要么被驱离（Hetherington 2019；Besky 2020）。正如印度活动家、学者万达娜·希瓦（Vandana Shiva 1993）所批判的，支撑这些相连过程的单一种植逻辑，无法容忍其他栽培或知识体系，其目的主要是经济主义的、反多元的。这种不宽容，包含了普遍的漠视：既漠视原住民与地方社群长期以来同环境及其超越人类居民建立关系的方式，也漠视当地人受文化与精神世界塑造的、体验、解释并介入快速变化景观的方式（Kröger 2022）。它还伴随着一种认识上的短视：看不到非人生命能够对人类驱动的项目施加自身影响与作用，乃至与之抗衡。害虫、寄生生物及其他野化生物的活动，正体现了这种能力——它们把资本主义的自然转作自己的家园与宿主（Tomich 2011；Ovstehage 2021）。

en: Initiatives that seek to enhance the sustainability of the plantation sector, yet that remain premised on top-down, technocratic epistemologies and praxiologies, can all too easily end up replicating the very same hierarchies and exclusions that lie at the heart of the plantation system itself – human/non-human, nature/culture, wild/domesticated, and so forth. This includes conservation practices that are predicated on the belief that biodiversity protection is best achieved by isolating ecosystems from humans, now reframed as sources of disturbance, and that therefore come to perpetuate the colonial paradigm of ‘fortress conservation’ (Brockington 2002; see also Milne 2022). The result is a form of sustainability that dispossesses and excludes local communities by conjuring natures worth preserving as pristine and untouched zones of ‘wilderness’, while simultaneously displacing and erasing place-based relationships, meanings, values, and histories (Cronon 1996; Tsing 2003). Such forms of sustainability constitute manifestations of ‘eco-imperialism’ (Driessen 2010) that further ‘accumulation through (double) dispossession’ (Harvey 2003) by failing to acknowledge the intrinsic engagement of humans with their environment and the encompassment of other-than-human lifeforms within the multispecies society that constitutes ‘nature’ itself. In designating only particular sites and landscapes as worthy of conserving, they elide critical local, relational, and holistic understandings of the landscape as a living whole – including the sometimes unexpected frictions and tensions that shape the material and moral relations of humans to non-humans.
zh: 那些试图提高种植园产业可持续性、却仍以自上而下的技术官僚式认识论与实践论为前提的倡议，非常容易最终复制种植园体系本身核心的等级与排斥：人类／非人、自然／文化、野生／驯化，等等。其中包括这样一些保护实践：它们相信，实现生物多样性保护的最佳方式，是将生态系统与人类隔离，把人重新界定为扰动来源，从而延续了“堡垒式保护”的殖民范式（Brockington 2002；另见Milne 2022）。结果便是一种剥夺并排斥当地社群的可持续性：它把值得保护的自然想象成纯净、未经触动的“荒野”，同时挤走并抹除植根于地方的关系、意义、价值和历史（Cronon 1996；Tsing 2003）。这些可持续性形式，体现了“生态帝国主义”（Driessen 2010），并进一步推动“通过（双重）剥夺而进行的积累”（Harvey 2003）：它们不承认人类与环境之间内在的相互参与，也不承认非人生命形式被包含于构成“自然”本身的多物种社会之中。它们只把特定地点与景观指定为值得保护的对象，从而遮蔽了一些关键的理解：地方性的、关系性的、整体性的理解，把景观看作一个活的整体，其中也包括那些有时出人意料、塑造人与非人之间物质及道德关系的摩擦与紧张。
